survey: A classic flying saucer seen from slightly above and to the front, tilted a little toward the viewer. Main parts: (1) The body is a wide, shallow cone of brushed steel. It rises from the outer rim to a raised collar in the middle. (2) The rim is a dark grey tube that runs all the way around the edge of the cone, closed and evenly elliptical in perspective. (3) The cockpit is a green glass dome sitting in a metal ring collar at the top of the cone. Its base ellipse matches the angle of the saucer, so it sits on the hull and doesn't float. (4) About ten orange lights are set into the rim tube, spaced evenly in perspective. They are closer together at the sides and further apart at the front, and on the far side they are hidden behind the dome. The saucer floats with no support, which is right for a flying craft. The underside and engines are not shown, which is an acceptable simplification. All parts are joined, nothing passes through anything else, and the shapes are round and even.
